title: Asked Three Ways
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 158
medium: Interactive page (index.html, SVG built in the browser): the visitor places their own reading of 'Probably' first; then, for 27 probability and quantity phrases, 46 people's answers as dots, twelve machine instances' answers as stacks, and two stated distributions as bands (six instances describing the people, six describing themselves); a switch marks where the family's centre differs from the people's. A figure (figure.svg); Python for briefs, scoring and a labelled post-hoc check; briefs, verbatim replies and predictions.
embodies: A machine judge's three relations to a norm, set side by side: performing it (twelve instances give one number, identical on 12 of 27 phrases), stating its own (asked about itself, it finds its centre), and describing the people's (it draws their spread and moves their centre onto its own on 10 of 11 phrases where the two differ, with the poll in recall).
result: P1 held (25 of 27). P2 held (25 of 27). P3 held (24 of 27). P4 failed (7 of 27; 14 needed). P5 failed (0 of 8; 5 needed). Post hoc, labelled: describers gave the people the family's centre on 10 of 11 diverging phrases.
project_step: Thirty-ninth experiment of the project. Operation: judging (with perceiving). Builds Session 157's proposed 'describer and sampler' and tests Session 155's ruling that the family cannot report its own norm from inside (not borne out: asked about itself it located its centre) and experiment 37's finding that its peak is its own (borne out in a new domain: its description of the people carries that peak). Works with and against Cartography, not Tracing (map as performance, tracing as alleged competence): here the competence is the performance laid on the people's spread.
material: zonination/perceptions (MIT licence): 46 people's numbers for 17 probability phrases and 10 quantity phrases, from an r/samplesize poll of 2015. Domain: the language of estimative uncertainty (verbal probability and vague quantity).
seed: prepare.py seed 158 (question orders); makers are model instances and not seeded
